slides.myth: A charger left in the wall with nothing on it uses no power.
slides.fact: Lots of plugged-in gear keeps sipping power on standby, chargers included. Standby use is estimated at about 5 to 10% of home electricity.

slides.myth: Every power strip protects your stuff from surges.
slides.fact: A basic power strip just gives you more outlets. Only a surge protector does that job. Look for "surge protector", a joule rating and a UL 1449 listing.
The parts inside wear out as they absorb surges, and many keep passing power after they stop protecting. If the "protected" light is out, replace it.
slides.source: Surge protector makers and buying guides

slides.myth: Running an extension cord under a rug is fine.
slides.fact: Covering a cord traps its heat and can start a fire, and foot traffic wears it down. Don't run cords under rugs, carpets or furniture.

slides.myth: If a breaker keeps tripping, just put in a bigger one.
slides.fact: The breaker is sized to protect the wires in the wall. A bigger one lets them overheat. Find what's overloading the circuit or call an electrician.
slides.source: CPSC electrical safety checklist, Indiana Electric Cooperatives
